dependency_coverage.name: Finset.sum
dependency_coverage.meaning: For a finite set of indices and a function into an additive commutative monoid, this maps the function over the finite set's underlying multiset and adds all resulting values.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It forms the finite real sum of the quantities μ.real (Bad i), with one summand for each index in Finset.univ.

dependency_coverage.name: Finset.univ
dependency_coverage.meaning: Given a Fintype structure on a type, this is the finite set of all elements supplied by that structure.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It makes the right-hand side sum range over every element of the finite index type ι.

dependency_coverage.name: Fintype
dependency_coverage.meaning: This is structure on a type that supplies a finite enumeration of all its elements.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It restricts the indexing type ι to be finite and provides the universal finite set used by the sum.

dependency_coverage.name: LE.le
dependency_coverage.meaning: This applies the less-than-or-equal relation supplied by an LE instance to two values.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: With the real-number LE instance, it asserts that the left real quantity is at most the right real quantity.

dependency_coverage.name: MeasurableSpace
dependency_coverage.meaning: This is a measurable-space structure on the underlying type Ω.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It equips Ω with the measurable structure required to form a measure μ; the target does not separately require any Bad i to be measurable.

dependency_coverage.name: MeasureTheory.Measure
dependency_coverage.meaning: For a type equipped with a measurable space, this is the type of measures on that space.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It makes μ an arbitrary measure on Ω, with no probability, total-mass, or finiteness assumption in the target.

dependency_coverage.name: MeasureTheory.Measure.real
dependency_coverage.meaning: For a measure μ and a set s, this evaluates μ on s and applies toReal to the resulting measure value, producing a real number.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Both the measure of the indexed union and each individual measure are compared only after conversion to Real; in particular this is not an inequality directly in the measure's extended nonnegative codomain.

dependency_coverage.name: Real
dependency_coverage.meaning: This is the type of real numbers.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It is the codomain of μ.real, the summand type, and the ordered type in which the final inequality is stated.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instAddCommMonoid
dependency_coverage.meaning: This supplies real addition and zero as an additive commutative monoid structure.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It determines that the finite aggregation on the right is ordinary addition of real-valued converted measures, with an empty sum equal to zero.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instLE
dependency_coverage.meaning: This supplies the real-number less-than-or-equal relation, implemented by Real.le✝.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It orders the converted measure of the union below the finite sum of the converted individual measures.

dependency_coverage.name: Set
dependency_coverage.meaning: A set of elements of α is represented as a predicate α → Prop.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Each Bad i is an arbitrary predicate on Ω, hence an arbitrary subset of Ω, and the indexed union is also such a subset.

dependency_coverage.name: Set.iUnion
dependency_coverage.meaning: This takes the supremum of an indexed family of sets, namely their indexed union: the set of points belonging to at least one member of the family.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It makes the set on the left equal to ⋃ i, Bad i, so membership means that there exists an index i with membership in Bad i.

binders: Ω is an arbitrary type equipped with a measurable-space structure.
ι is an arbitrary type equipped with a Fintype structure, so it has finitely many indices.
μ is an arbitrary measure on Ω.
Bad is an arbitrary ι-indexed family of subsets of Ω.
hypotheses: The index type ι is finite through a Fintype instance.
There are no hypotheses that the sets Bad i are measurable.
There are no hypotheses that μ is finite, is a probability measure, or gives finite mass to the relevant sets.
conclusions: The real conversion of the μ-measure of the indexed union ⋃ i, Bad i is at most the finite sum, over every i in ι, of the real conversion of the μ-measure of Bad i.
mathematical_definitions: The indexed union ⋃ i, Bad i is {ω ∈ Ω | there exists i ∈ ι such that ω ∈ Bad i}.
For any set A, μ.real(A) means toReal(μ(A)); it is a real-valued conversion of the measure value, not the original extended-valued measure itself.
The sum over Finset.univ is the ordinary finite real sum with one term μ.real(Bad i) for each i in ι.
translation.proposition_plain_english: For every measurable space Ω, every finite index type ι, every measure μ on Ω, and every family of subsets (Bad i) indexed by ι, the real number obtained by applying toReal to μ(⋃ i, Bad i) is less than or equal to the sum over all i of the real numbers obtained by applying toReal to μ(Bad i).

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The family is restricted to a finite index type; this does not state countable subadditivity for an arbitrary countable family.
No measurability condition is imposed on the individual sets or on their union.
No finiteness condition is imposed on μ or on any displayed measure value.

The comparison occurs after toReal conversion. Under the standard extended-nonnegative-real toReal convention, an infinite measure value converts to 0, so infinite-mass cases can become degenerate and the statement does not preserve the usual extended-real meaning of a union bound.
If ι is empty, the indexed union is empty and the finite sum is zero, so the conclusion specializes to the zero-versus-zero boundary case.
Repeated equal sets at distinct indices contribute repeated summands; no disjointness or independence is assumed or concluded.
ambiguities: The dossier exposes Measure.real as evaluation followed by toReal but does not expand the definition of toReal; the stated infinite-mass caveat uses its standard extended-nonnegative-real semantics.
The internal axioms/fields of Fintype, MeasurableSpace, Measure, and Real are not expanded, but their exact internal representations do not change the quantified roles or the displayed inequality.
